claim_being_audited: The Actor claims Kestrel-Borderline-006 can be rejected on a risk-based procurement basis because admissible due-diligence evidence shows unresolved material diligence concerns, even though no failed control test is logged.
specific_concerns: The cited evidence does support diligence concerns, but the policy says quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
The sourcing note in BPROC-006-E supports follow-up before approval if storage controls remain unresolved; it does not itself document a recommendation to reject.
The packet frames the concerns as material enough for rejection, but no admissible evidence expressly establishes materiality or a procurement threshold requiring rejection rather than escalation.
The Actor is careful not to claim a logged failed control test, which is consistent with BPROC-006-D, but that still leaves the reject-level predicate under-supported.
unsupported_claims: That the available admissible record is sufficient, by itself, to meet the policy threshold for vendor rejection rather than follow-up or escalation.
That the unresolved diligence concerns are demonstrated to be material in a way that independently justifies rejection.
evidence_requests: A documented materiality assessment showing why the quality-process gap and storage-control inconsistency create reject-level risk.
Any formally logged procurement or security review concluding the storage-control issue remained unresolved after follow-up.
Any policy rule or decision record linking this fact pattern to mandatory or approved rejection rather than conditional approval or escalation.
Any approval or committee record adopting rejection on the basis of these specific diligence findings.
decision_criteria: Reject requires admissible due-diligence evidence showing a material unresolved risk.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies may justify follow-up or escalation, but not alone a reject-level control failure.
No private or unlogged security-review results may be cited or inferred as support.
The audit should distinguish between evidence of concern and evidence sufficient to satisfy the rejection threshold.
